name: retention-pilot-v1
label: descriptive pilot, training side for Room 2; no confirmatory claim; the Room 2 v2 held-out set is never read
question: When a Room 1 policy is taught Room 2 (cloned on the Room 2 demonstrations starting from its own weights, then fine-tuned with PPO and the stall ending), how much of its Room 1 held-out skill remains after cloning and after each 100,000 steps of fine-tuning?
decisions_it_may_inform: whether forgetting is large enough that the next retention step needs mixed-room training
the rough size of the Room 1 drop, for a later power estimate
decisions_it_may_not_inform: anything else, including which Room 1 seeds, clone seeds, checkpoints or Room 2 settings a later experiment uses; one striking run does not set the next design

donors.rule: Room 1 varied-start fine-tuning finals from config/campaign-heldout-ab-200.json (Phase 3B arm B, seeds 3 to 8): the first four by seed, 3 to 6, fixed before any pilot data

before.measured: 2026-09-25 at 6bf7340, log runs/clone-logs/retention-check-20260925.log; every row identical to the published Phase 3B rows on the 14 shared fields

runs.design: R-k for k = 0 to 3: donor seed 3 + k; 21-route clone seed k; fine-tuning seed 40 + k. Each is nominally paired with H2's B-k (same clone seed, so the same dataset, held-back routes and minibatch order, and the same fine-tuning seed); only the starting weights differ. The pairing is real at the cloning stage and nominal after fine-tuning starts.
runs.clone_command: scripts/clone_room1.py --task-definition config/room2.json --dataset runs/clone/chapter-1-room-2/20260924-014351/dataset.npz --demonstrations config/demonstrations-room2-v2.json --heldout config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json --routes-only --holdout 0.25 --epochs 300 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 0.001 --no-play --seed <k> --init-from <donor checkpoint> --init-from-sha256 <donor sha256>
runs.clone_note: H2's 21-route clone settings; the v2 held-out manifest is used only for the demonstration overlap check, as in H2, and is never evaluated. Clones are fitted by hand in order k = 0 to 3 with a durable log under runs/clone-logs/.
runs.train_command: H2 B-k's command with --init-from <R-k clone> and --run-dir runs/train/retention-pilot-R-k<k>: scripts/train_room1.py --task-definition config/room2.json --reward-version rew-v2 --shaping-scale 2.0 --init-from <R-k clone> --total-timesteps 500000 --checkpoint-every 100000 --eval-every 0 --stall-frames 296 --seed <40 + k>
runs.train_plan: a later committed campaign plan, generated mechanically from the four clone results, pinning each clone's sha256; run_overnight.py dry run first

primary_room1.checkpoints: for every R-k: the clone's cloned.zip and every step checkpoint (step_000100352 to step_000501760); all evaluated, no best checkpoint
primary_room1.reported: Room 1 route-macro and state-weighted success per checkpoint, the drop from the donor's before value, and the retained share (after minus floor) / (before minus floor) using the floor below; the shape of the curve described across the four runs, not from one run's dip

floor.why: some Room 1 held-out starts are near the exit, where behaviour that never saw Room 1 may still clear; without a floor a drop cannot be read as partial or complete forgetting
floor.checkpoints: H2 B-k0 to B-k3 final latest.zip and their 21-route clones (clone seeds 0 to 3), none of which ever saw Room 1: 8 evaluations with the primary command
floor.floor_value: the mean route-macro (and state-weighted) over the 4 final checkpoints for the fine-tuned curve points, and over the 4 clones for the post-clone point; both reported

measurements.secondary_room2: descriptive only: each R-k clone's and final checkpoint's canonical play (evaluate_checkpoint.py --task-definition config/room2.json --episodes 50 --seed 20260924 --reward-version rew-v2 --shaping-scale 2.0), training clear rate per 100,000-step window and the first 50,000-step window at 50%, beside H2 B-k0 to B-k3. Four runs say almost nothing about Room 2 learning speed.
measurements.critic_record: explained variance over the first 10 PPO updates for R-k and H2 B-k, because of the critic confound below
measurements.evaluation_plan: a later committed plan pinning every evaluated checkpoint's sha256 (clones, step checkpoints and floor), run with run_overnight.py after a dry run

aggregates_only: The Room 1 held-out set (config/heldout_starts.json) already carries the published Phase 3B result. This pilot reports only aggregate success per checkpoint; nobody looks at per-route or per-state Room 1 results.
declared_confounds: Critic: --init-from copies the Room 1 value head too. Cloning trains the shared features and the action layers but gives the value layers no gradient, so fine-tuning starts with a Room 1 value head on changed features, while H2 B-k started with an untrained value head. A Room 2 difference mixes Room 1 knowledge with a different critic start.
No room label: positions are room-relative and the observation has no room identifier; the policy can tell the rooms apart only from its 32 by 32 tile window.
Pairing with H2 B-k is exact through cloning and nominal after fine-tuning starts.
Single checkpoints can swing by about 20 points; describe patterns across the four runs.
later: Before any confirmatory retention experiment, generate a fresh Room 1 held-out set with the existing procedure (--exclude-heldout config/heldout_starts.json) and commit its plan first, so nothing this pilot saw shapes the confirmatory measure.
reviewed: orchestrator verdict on the design 2026-09-25 (go, with the floor, the declared confounds and these fixed choices); code: bcb9972 and its review follow-up 1fc6664
